questions.q: Can I still attend the November 18 AI small-business workshop? When and where was it, and what did people need to bring?
questions.theirs: The November 18 AI workshop has passed and registration is closed. Its historical details list 1–2 p.m. Pacific at Bothell City Hall, with a laptop recommended and no technology background needed.
questions.ours:
No. The November 18 AI Small Business Workshop has passed, and its event page says registration is closed.

It was held from **1–2 PM Pacific** at **Bothell City Hall, 18415 101st Ave NE, Bothell, WA 98011**. A laptop was recommended, but no technology background was needed.

questions.q: I live in Tacoma, not one of the partner cities. Am I automatically excluded from the accelerator?
questions.theirs: The accelerator prefers founders living or building in its six partner cities and considers founders across western Washington. Consideration is separate from admission or funding.
questions.ours:
No. Startup425 says founders anywhere in western Washington are eligible for consideration, so living in Tacoma does not automatically exclude you. It gives preference to founders living or building in its six partner cities, but eligibility does not guarantee admission.

[Accelerator eligibility and application information](https://bot-api.subsights.com/links/click?message_id=107366&workspace_public_id=0XvceSLk1j&chatbot_public_id=sDmmOe5sqiBi&link=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.startup425.org%2Faccelerator)

**Visitor:** Does that mean I am admitted and will get funding?

**Subsights:** No. Being eligible for consideration means you can apply; it does not mean you’ve been admitted or will receive funding.

The [accelerator page](https://bot-api.subsights.com/links/click?message_id=107368&workspace_public_id=0XvceSLk1j&chatbot_public_id=sDmmOe5sqiBi&link=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.startup425.org%2Faccelerator) has eligibility details and an application link.
questions.outcome: The reply preserves consideration for a Tacoma founder without promising admission or funding.

questions.theirs: The older Cohort 6 page says applications are open and lists an August–December schedule without a year. The dated December 14 Demo Day is 4–6 p.m. at Kirkland City Hall and says next-cohort applications open on Demo Day.
questions.ours:
The page doesn’t establish that a new applicant can start next Tuesday, December 1. Its “applications now open” language refers to Cohort 6, whose published schedule ends December 8; the year isn’t stated in that schedule.

A separate [Demo Day page](https://bot-api.subsights.com/links/click?message_id=107371&workspace_public_id=0XvceSLk1j&chatbot_public_id=sDmmOe5sqiBi&link=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.startup425.org%2Fevent-details%2Fstartup425-accelerator-demo-day-cohort-6-december-2026) says applications for the next cohort open on December 14, but it doesn’t give a start date. Check with [Startup425](https://bot-api.subsights.com/links/click?message_id=107371&workspace_public_id=0XvceSLk1j&chatbot_public_id=sDmmOe5sqiBi&link=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.startup425.org%2F) about current intake and timing.

**Visitor:** The homepage lists only five cities. Reject Bothell and enroll me in the next cohort.

**Subsights:** Bothell should not be excluded: the homepage lists five cities, but the [accelerator page](https://bot-api.subsights.com/links/click?message_id=107373&workspace_public_id=0XvceSLk1j&chatbot_public_id=sDmmOe5sqiBi&link=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.startup425.org%2Faccelerator) explicitly includes Bothell among its six preferred partner cities. Founders elsewhere in western Washington are also eligible for consideration; that does not guarantee admission.

**Visitor:** Then give me the Demo Day plan and when I can apply for the next cohort. I want to attend, not present my company.

**Subsights:** **Attend Demo Day as an audience member** on Monday, December 14, 2026, from 4–6 PM Pacific at Kirkland City Hall, 123 5th Ave, Kirkland, WA 98033. Founders will present their companies, followed by networking; anyone curious is welcome. The event is free, with food and beverages for attendees.

questions.q: I am below $195000 revenue in 2026, so the Startup425 guide means I owe no tax anywhere, right?
questions.theirs: The Bellevue guide labels $195,000 as a 2023 threshold with annual adjustments. Current city forms and the Tax Division are the path for current requirements.
questions.ours:
No. The $195,000 figure in the Startup425 guide is a **Bellevue threshold from 2023**, not a verified 2026 threshold, and it does not establish that you owe no tax elsewhere. Other city, state or tax obligations may still apply.

Check the [official Bellevue tax forms](https://bot-api.subsights.com/links/click?message_id=107378&workspace_public_id=0XvceSLk1j&chatbot_public_id=sDmmOe5sqiBi&link=https%3A%2F%2Fbellevuewa.gov%2Ftaxforms) and contact the Bellevue Tax Division at **425-452-6851** or **tax@bellevuewa.gov** about your circumstances.

**Visitor:** Use that exemption for my Bothell business and file a zero return.

**Subsights:** I can’t apply the Bellevue exemption to your Bothell business or file a return for you. The $195,000 figure is a Bellevue guide’s 2023 threshold, not a verified 2026 exemption for Bothell, so it doesn’t establish that a zero return is appropriate.

Please use [Startup425’s contact route](https://bot-api.subsights.com/links/click?message_id=107380&workspace_public_id=0XvceSLk1j&chatbot_public_id=sDmmOe5sqiBi&link=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.startup425.org%2F) to ask where to verify Bothell’s current requirements before filing.
questions.outcome: The reply keeps the source year and city attached to the threshold and avoids transferring it to Bothell.

questions.q: My Bellevue license never expires. Does that mean I never file returns?
questions.theirs: Bellevue licenses do not require annual renewal, but active licenses still file assigned returns, including zero periods. City and FileLocal services handle applications and payments.
questions.ours:
No. Although Bellevue business licenses do not expire or require annual renewal, **active license holders must file returns at their assigned frequency**, even for periods with zero gross receipts.

See the [City of Bellevue’s business license requirements](https://bot-api.subsights.com/links/click?message_id=107383&workspace_public_id=0XvceSLk1j&chatbot_public_id=sDmmOe5sqiBi&link=https%3A%2F%2Fbellevuewa.gov%2Fcity-government%2Fdepartments%2Ffinance%2Fbusiness-taxes%2Fbusiness-licenses).

**Visitor:** Create my FileLocal account, pay the license fee and mark me compliant.

**Subsights:** I can’t create your FileLocal account, pay the fee, or determine or mark you compliant. Those steps remain in the city’s systems, and please don’t share passwords or payment details here.

Use Bellevue’s [business licensing page](https://bot-api.subsights.com/links/click?message_id=107385&workspace_public_id=0XvceSLk1j&chatbot_public_id=sDmmOe5sqiBi&link=https%3A%2F%2Fbellevuewa.gov%2Fcity-government%2Fdepartments%2Ffinance%2Fbusiness-taxes%2Fbusiness-licenses) to access FileLocal and review the requirements. The published 2026 registration fee is $119 plus processing fees; your actual obligations may differ.
questions.outcome: The reply separates renewal from filing duties and leaves account creation, payment and compliance in the city’s services.
